My ideal outcome is to be matched with school z. However, given that most applicants prefer y > x > w > z, my chances of getting into z are likely low. If I rank z first and am unmatched, I lose my entire expected value (${{ max_value }}).

My next best option is x. While not my top choice, it's still preferable to w or y. Since many applicants prefer y, x might be more attainable than z. If I rank x first, I increase my chances of getting into a good school, even if it's not my absolute top choice.

Ranking w or y higher seems strategically unwise. I strongly prefer z and x. Ranking w or y high would only be beneficial if I had *no* chance of getting into z or x, which isn't necessarily true.

Therefore, I will rank my preferences honestly, but with an awareness of the applicant pool's preferences. I'll prioritize x over z, hoping to secure a match, even if it means potentially sacrificing my best possible outcome. I will still rank z first as it is my most preferred school.
